title: GENERAL STANDARDS FOR SOUND FAMILY RITES
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe the contents of the General Standards for Sound Family Rites and matters concerning their dissemination and observance under Article 5 (4) of the Act on Family Rite Establishment and Related Assistance.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Decree are defined as follows:
1. "Coming-of-age rites" means ceremonial procedures performed to foster awareness of the social responsibilities of an adult.
2. "Wedding rites" means ceremonial procedures from engagement or marriage through sinhaeng, the traditional post-marriage journey of a newlywed to the spouse's home.
3. "Funeral rites" means ceremonial procedures from the time of dying until the end of mourning.
4. "Ancestral memorial rites" means the ceremonial procedures of annual death-anniversary rites and memorial rites performed on traditional holidays (hereinafter referred to as "holiday memorial rites").
5. "Longevity birthday rites" means ceremonial procedures performed to commemorate birthdays from the age of 60 onward.
6. "Chief mourner" means the person who presides over the ceremonial procedures of funeral rites.
7. "Memorial-rite officiant" means the person who presides over the ceremonial procedures of ancestral memorial rites.

Article 3 (Special Provisions for Religious Ceremonies)
Where family rites are performed in accordance with religious ceremonies, the procedures particular to the relevant religion may be followed within the limits of the General Standards for Sound Family Rites prescribed in this Decree.

Article 4 (Dissemination and Observance of the General Standards for Sound Family Rites)
The heads of state agencies, local governments, public institutions and organizations, business enterprises, and similar bodies may encourage public officials, executive officers, employees, and others under their authority to observe the General Standards for Sound Family Rites, or may establish and disseminate practices for their observance.

CHAPTER II COMING-OF-AGE RITES

Article 5 (Timing)
Coming-of-age rites may be performed once a person has attained the full age of 19 years.

Article 6 (Coming-of-Age Rites)
(1) Where state agencies, local governments, public institutions and organizations, business enterprises, and similar bodies hold coming-of-age ceremonies, they shall do so solemnly and simply.
(2) The order of a coming-of-age ceremony, the coming-of-age oath, and the declaration of adulthood shall be as set out in Annex 1.

CHAPTER III WEDDING RITES

Article 7 (Engagement)
(1) On engagement, only the parties to the engagement and their immediate families, such as their parents, shall attend a meeting of the two families and discuss all matters concerning the marriage; no separate engagement ceremony shall be held.
(2) In the case prescribed in paragraph (1), the parties to the engagement shall exchange the engagement agreement in Annex 2, attaching the following documents:
1. Medical examination certificates of the parties;
2. Some or all of the certificates specified in the subparagraphs of Article 15 (1) of the Act on Registration of Family Relations (to be attached only where necessary as agreed by the parties).

Article 8 (Marriage)
(1) The following shall be observed when a wedding ceremony is held:
1. The venue shall be the home of either party to the marriage, a wedding hall, or another place suitable for a sound wedding ceremony;
2. The parties to the marriage shall sign or affix their seals to the marriage report;
3. Wedding attire shall be neat, simple, and clean;
4. Invitations shall be kept modest and extended mainly to relatives by blood and marriage.
(2) The trousseau and other goods prepared for marriage shall be modest and practical; where customary wedding gifts are sent, they shall be sent only to the parents of the parties to the marriage.
(3) A reception following the wedding ceremony shall be simple, with relatives by blood and marriage as the principal guests.
(4) The order of a wedding ceremony, the marriage vows, and the declaration of marriage shall be as set out in Annex 3.

CHAPTER IV FUNERAL RITES

Article 9 (Funeral Rites)
The ceremonies performed after death until burial or cremation is completed shall comprise the departure ceremony and the ceremony for the repose of the spirit. Other ceremonies, namely the roadside rite, the rite on returning from the burial place, and the memorial rite on the third day after the funeral, may be omitted.

Article 10 (Departure Ceremony)
(1) The departure ceremony shall be held at the bereaved family's home or the funeral hall immediately before the coffin containing the body leaves that home or funeral hall. <Amended on July 2, 2019>
(2) The coffin shall be placed at the venue of the departure ceremony, and candlesticks, an incense burner, an incense box, and other similar items shall be prepared.

Article 11 (Ceremony for the Repose of the Spirit)
The ceremony for the repose of the spirit shall be conducted as follows: <Amended on July 2, 2019>
1. In the case of burial: After the grave mound has been completed, a portrait of the deceased shall be placed and simple ritual offerings laid out, followed, in order, by the burning of incense, an offering of an alcoholic beverage, the reading of an invocation, and ceremonial bows.
2. In the case of cremation: After cremation has been completed, the urn containing the remains shall be placed and procedures corresponding to those in subparagraph 1 shall be followed.

Article 12 (Day of Burial or Cremation)
Except in unavoidable circumstances, burial or cremation shall take place on the third day counting from the day of death. <Amended on July 2, 2019>

Article 13 (Period of Mourning)
(1) The period of mourning for parents, grandparents, and a spouse shall extend to the 100th day counting from the day of death; for other persons, it shall extend to the day of burial or cremation. <Amended on July 2, 2019>
(2) No temporary altar for enshrining the spirit tablet during the period of mourning shall be set up; the ceremony ending mourning shall follow procedures corresponding to the annual death-anniversary rite.

Article 14 (Mourning Attire)
(1) Mourning attire shall not be specially procured. Where Korean traditional attire is worn, it shall be white; where Western attire is worn, it shall be black. A mourning badge shall be worn on the chest, or a mourning hood shall be worn; provided, ordinary clothing may be worn in unavoidable circumstances.
(2) Mourning attire shall be worn until the day of burial or cremation, and a mourning badge shall be worn until mourning ends. <Amended on July 2, 2019>

Article 15 (Mourners)
(1) The spouse and lineal descendants of the deceased shall be the mourners, that is, the persons in mourning. <Amended on July 2, 2019>
(2) The spouse or the eldest son shall serve as chief mourner.
(3) Where the deceased has no descendants, the nearest relative shall preside over the funeral rites.

Article 16 (Obituary Notices)
Where an obituary notice is published in a newspaper, the name of an administrative agency or a public institution or organization shall not be used.

Article 17 (Funeral Procession)
The funeral procession shall proceed in the order of the memorial banner bearing the deceased's name, the portrait of the deceased, the coffin, the mourners, and the persons attending to offer condolences. Where a bier is used, it shall not be excessively decorated.

Article 18 (Order of the Departure Ceremony)
The order of the departure ceremony and the specifications of the mourning badge shall be as set out in Annex 4.

CHAPTER V ANCESTRAL MEMORIAL RITES

Article 19 (Categories of Ancestral Memorial Rites)
Ancestral memorial rites shall be divided into annual death-anniversary rites and holiday memorial rites.

Article 20 (Annual Death-Anniversary Rites)
(1) Annual death-anniversary rites shall be performed for ancestors up to the second generation above the memorial-rite officiant.
(2) An annual death-anniversary rite shall be performed at the memorial-rite officiant's home each year on the day on which the ancestor died.

Article 21 (Holiday Memorial Rites)
(1) Holiday memorial rites shall be performed for the ancestors for whom annual death-anniversary rites are performed.
(2) Holiday memorial rites shall be performed at the eldest grandson's home on the morning of each traditional holiday every year.

Article 22 (Ritual Offerings)
Ritual offerings shall be arranged naturally, using the simple dishes of an ordinary meal.

Article 23 (Procedures for Ancestral Memorial Rites)
The procedures for ancestral memorial rites shall be as set out in Annex 5.

Article 24 (Visits to Ancestral Graves)
Visits to ancestral graves shall be made at each person's convenience; ritual offerings shall either not be prepared or be kept simple.

CHAPTER VI LONGEVITY BIRTHDAY RITES

Article 25 (Sixtieth-Birthday Banquets and Similar Celebrations)
Longevity birthday rites, such as sixtieth- and seventieth-birthday banquets, shall be held simply at home with relatives and close acquaintances gathered together.

ADDENDUM <Presidential Decree No. 21083, October 14, 2008>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDUM (Decree Partially Amending the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Excavation of the Remains of Soldiers Killed in the Korean War and Other Decrees to Minimize the Collection of Resident Registration Numbers) <Presidential Decree No. 26774, December 30, 2015>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation. <Proviso omitted>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation. <Proviso omitted>

ANNEX 1 <Amended on July 2, 2019>
Order of Coming-of-Age Ceremonies, Coming-of-Age Oath, and Declaration of Adulthood (Related to Article 6 (2))

1. Order of coming-of-age ceremonies

(a) Individual coming-of-age ceremony
1) Opening
2) Ceremonial bow by the person coming of age
3) Congratulatory address
4) Coming-of-age oath and signature
5) Declaration of adulthood and signature
6) Chorye (a coming-of-age observance in which an alcoholic beverage is drunk and instruction is given in proper drinking conduct) and an admonitory address by the officiant
7) Ceremonial bow by the person coming of age
8) Closing

(b) Group coming-of-age ceremony
1) Opening
2) National ceremonial observances
3) Calling the names of the persons coming of age
4) Salute by the persons coming of age
5) Admonitory address by the officiant
6) Coming-of-age oath and signature
7) Declaration of adulthood and signature
8) Congratulatory addresses by invited guests and responses
9) Salute by the persons coming of age to the invited guests
10) Closing

2. Coming-of-age oath

COMING-OF-AGE OATH

As I now come of age, I solemnly swear to be grateful to my ancestors and parents, whose kindness has brought me to this day, and to fulfill my duties as their descendant; and, as a member responsible for the State and society, to exercise my rightful entitlements, faithfully discharge my sacred obligations, and fulfill my responsibilities as an adult.

Year ______  Month ______  Day ______

Person coming of age: ○ ○ ○ (Signature or seal)

3. Declaration of adulthood

DECLARATION OF ADULTHOOD

Person coming of age: ○ ○ ○
Date of birth: Year ______  Month ______  Day ______

As you now come of age, you have pledged and signed that you will fulfill your duties as a descendant and, as a member responsible for the State and society, faithfully uphold your rightful entitlements and sacred obligations. I therefore solemnly declare that you have attained adulthood.

Year ______  Month ______  Day ______

Officiant: ○ ○ ○ (Signature or seal)

ANNEX 2 <Amended on January 5, 2021>
Engagement Agreement (Related to Article 7 (2))

ENGAGEMENT AGREEMENT

| Name | __________________ | __________________ |

The two persons named above promise to marry on the following terms:
1. Intended date of marriage: __________________
2. Other conditions: __________________

Year ______  Month ______  Day ______

Parties to the engagement:
(Man) ○ ○ ○ (Signature or seal)
(Woman) ○ ○ ○ (Signature or seal)

Witnesses:
(For the man) Address: __________________
Name: ○ ○ ○ (Signature or seal)
(For the woman) Address: __________________
Name: ○ ○ ○ (Signature or seal)

Attachments:
1. One copy of a medical examination certificate;
2. Some or all of the certificates specified in the subparagraphs of Article 15 (1) of the Act on Registration of Family Relations (to be attached only where necessary as agreed by the parties).

Note: Where consent under Article 808 of the Civil Act is required, the witness shall be the person entitled to give that consent.

ANNEX 3
Order of Wedding Ceremonies, Marriage Vows, and Declaration of Marriage (Related to Article 8 (4))

1. Order of a wedding ceremony
(a) Opening
(b) Entrance of the groom
(c) Entrance of the bride
(d) Mutual bow by the groom and bride
(e) Marriage vows and signatures
(f) Declaration of marriage
(g) Address by the officiant
(h) Greetings to the parents of both families
(i) Greetings by the groom and bride to the invited guests
(j) Procession of the groom and bride
(k) Closing

2. Marriage vows

MARRIAGE VOWS

Taking Ms. ○○○ (or Mr. ○○○) as my wife (or husband), I vow always to love and respect her (or him) in all circumstances, to honor our elders, and to fulfill my duties as a faithful husband (or wife), thereby building a happy family.

Year ______  Month ______  Day ______
○○○ (Signature or seal)

3. Declaration of marriage

DECLARATION OF MARRIAGE

The groom, Mr. ○○○, and the bride, Ms. ○○○, have now solemnly vowed to become husband and wife in the presence of their families, relatives, and friends. Accordingly, as officiant, I solemnly declare that this marriage has been duly concluded.

Year ______  Month ______  Day ______
Officiant: ○○○ (Signature or seal)

ANNEX 4
Order of the Departure Ceremony and Specifications of the Mourning Badge (Related to Article 18)

1. Order of the departure ceremony
(a) Opening
(b) Burning of incense by the chief mourner and the mourners
(c) Offering of an alcoholic beverage
(d) Eulogy
(e) Burning of incense by the persons attending to offer condolences
(f) Salute by all present
(g) Closing

2. Specifications of the mourning badge
(a) Size of the cloth: 3 cm high × 5 cm wide; two layers shall be used.
(b) Folded shape: as shown in figure (b) below.

ANNEX 5 <Amended on July 2, 2019>
Procedures for Ancestral Memorial Rites (Related to Article 23)

1. General procedures
(a) Enshrining the spirit: After burning incense, the memorial-rite officiant pours an alcoholic beverage onto the mosa (sand placed in a bowl with a bundle of cogongrass inserted into it), and all participants bow twice together before the spirit tablet.
(b) Offering an alcoholic beverage: The alcoholic beverage is offered once.
(c) Reading the invocation: The invocation is read, followed by a moment of silent tribute.
(d) Parting bows: All participants bow twice before the spirit tablet.

2. Enshrining the spirit
A photograph shall serve as the representation of the spirit; where there is no photograph, a paper spirit tablet shall be used instead. The inscription on the paper tablet shall be written in Hangul on white paper using ink or similar material, as follows.

(a) For parents

| Father's tablet | Mother's tablet |
| --- | --- |
| 아버님 신위 | 어머님 ○○○○ 신위 |
| Spirit of Father | Spirit of Mother ○○○○ |

(b) For a spouse

| Husband's tablet | Wife's tablet |
| --- | --- |
| 부군 신위 | 부인 ○○○○ 신위 |
| Spirit of Husband | Spirit of Wife ○○○○ |

(c) For holiday memorial rites (joint ancestral rites)

| First column | Second column | Third column | Fourth column |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 할아버님 신위 | 할머님 ○○○○ 신위 | 아버님 신위 | 어머님 ○○○○ 신위 |
| Spirit of Grandfather | Spirit of Grandmother ○○○○ | Spirit of Father | Spirit of Mother ○○○○ |

Note: Enter the ancestral clan origin and the surname in the spaces marked ○○○○ on the paper spirit tablet.

[Translation note: The Hangul inscriptions above are retained as the prescribed examples, with their meanings translated immediately below. Each inscription in the original is written vertically from top to bottom; the column order of the joint tablet is preserved here from left to right.]
